# EGM Drift Report — 2026-11-05

* **Scope:** the five EGM contracts generated by `egm-bootstrap` on 2026-11-05 (EGM.md, blog/, case-studies/, docs/, dev-archive/)
* **Method:** five fresh-context Goldfish auditors (one per contract), each verifying every documented symbol, line citation, count, and invariant against current source
* **Reviewer accounting:** spawned 5 / completed 5 / not run 0

## EGM.md

- Page count wrong: root holds **17** HTML files, not 41 (41 was the whole-repo total). Build outputs 36 pages (17 root + 8 blog + 11 case-studies). Root also ships `theme-lab.html` (dev page) and `googleb057abba7f039342.html` (Google verification), undocumented.
- Title-suffix invariant false: no site-wide ` | Groundwork Landscaping` convention exists. Root pages mostly use `— Groundwork Landscaping` (em dash); the two root service-area pages use ` | Groundwork`; blog and all 11 case studies use ` | Groundwork` (no "Landscaping"); index/contact/theme-lab have none.
- `check_links.py` list omitted `parse_page` (line 109) plus case-mismatch detection, orphan reporting, and CSS `url()`/ld+json scanning.
- `build.py` list omitted `_run_pdf_writer` (line 419) and the PDF mechanism (weasyprint with `/tmp/pdfgen` venv fallback). "Five flyer PDFs" wrong — two are flyers; realtor counter card and two quote worksheets are not. mtime guard (line 447) means only stale PDFs regenerate, not "every build".
- Undocumented `build_html` transforms: inline `<style>` extraction+minify+reinject (376–379), stripping of hand-written `/site.css`+`/site.js` refs (374–375), Google Fonts link stripping (382), `ICON_TAGS` injection (116–119, applied 387).
- `asset_version` citation range wrong: ends at 106, not 113 (109–113 is `asset_tags`).
- `dev.py` rebuild call misquoted (actual: `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / "build.py")], check=True)`); undocumented argv port override (59) and 20-port probe window (21).
- "JS only wires behaviour" for the mobile CTA inexact: `ensureMobileCta` (244–258) builds the whole bar if `#mobile-cta` is absent.
- fonts/: three woff2 files but only two preloaded (`fraunces-italic-var.woff2` has no preload).
- netlify.toml undocumented beyond caching: security headers (X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy), HTML must-revalidate, `/img/*` immutable.
- Undersold `site.js`: `enhanceKeyboardAccess` (270) also does lightbox dialog semantics, focus traps, Escape handling, keyboard gallery activation (282–332); `initializeContactForm` (3) intercepts submit and posts via `fetch()` with success/error boxes and `aria-invalid` state (58–97).

## blog/README.md

- Overview said "eight posts plus the index" — actually **seven** posts + index (8 files); contradicted the contract's own Interface section.
- Title convention wrong: blog titles end ` | Groundwork`, not ` | Groundwork Landscaping`.
- `case_label` claim wrong on both counts: it runs only on case-studies pages (guard at build.py:152), never blog; and OG/twitter injection copies the full `<title>` verbatim (build.py:209, 289) — no suffix splitting.
- Post-imagery invariant doesn't hold: `img/blog/` contains zero `.jpg` — all `.webp`; two pages also pull imagery from `img/case-studies/*.webp`.

## case-studies/README.md

- Label invariant named the wrong suffix: pages end ` | Groundwork`, not ` | Groundwork Landscaping`.
- Gallery convention wrong on three counts: paths are root-absolute `/img/case-studies/...` (no `../img/`); all 142 references are `.webp` (zero `.jpg`); only 7 of 11 pages use the `<slug>/N-<description>` layout — three use flat unnumbered files (river-rock-parking-pad, front-yard-xeriscape, seasonal-landscape-cleanup) and `cedar-privacy-fence.html` borrows `lafayette-cedar-fence/`.

## docs/README.md

- Minor: `docs/marketing/qr-fall-page.png` not covered by the directory description.

## dev-archive/README.md

- Unlisted hidden dir: `.freebuff/` (tool artifact, one `project-id` file; already special-cased by `check_links.py` line 150).
- Side-effects claim imprecise: the 9 `.py` fixers anchor on `dev-archive/` itself (`BASE_DIR`), so run today they touch nothing outside it; the 10 `.sh` fixers use relative globs and would rewrite site HTML if run from the repo root.

## For human triage (not auto-fixed)

- Root `README.md` (hand-maintained): its photo drop-off conventions specified
  `.jpg` under `img/case-studies/<slug>/N-<description>.jpg`, but the pages
  actually use root-absolute `.webp` paths with mixed layouts.
  **RESOLVED 2026-11-05** — conventions section corrected with user approval
  (webp + `-800` variants committed, no build-time generation, About-page
  stand-in path fixed, `img/about/` marked as not-yet-existing).

## Remediation

All findings above were applied as corrections to the four affected contracts (EGM.md rewritten; blog, case-studies, docs, dev-archive patched) on 2026-11-05, except the human-triage item. Root `README.md` untouched.

## Round 3 — 2026-11-05

* **Method:** five fresh Goldfish auditors, same scope; round-2 additions (dead CSS claim, plan dates) explicitly targeted for verification.
* **Reviewer accounting:** spawned 5 / completed 5 / not run 0.

| Contract | Result |
| --- | --- |
| EGM.md | No drift detected |
| blog/README.md | 2 findings (below) |
| case-studies/README.md | 3 findings (below) |
| docs/README.md | No drift detected |
| dev-archive/README.md | No drift detected |

- **blog:** `site.css` lines 75–207 are a dead legacy fold-in for blog pages (scoped to `.blog-post-1`–`.blog-post-6` / `.blog-index` classes no element carries; pages styled by their own inline `<style>` blocks with element selectors; `blog-post-7.html` has no fold-in). Also: each blog page declares a dark `:root` palette that is inert in `dist/` because the build emits the page `<style>` before the `site.css` link, so site.css's light `:root` shadows it. Both documented in the contract.
- **case-studies:** (1) **Runtime bug found** — `seasonal-landscape-cleanup.html` line 326 has a legacy `onclick` lightbox call with a relative path; the build carries it verbatim into `data-lightbox-src`, which resolves against `/case-studies/` and 404s at runtime. Verified in source and dist. Documented as a flagged exception; fixing the page is production code and left for human triage. (2) Round 2's site.css description was wrong: six blocks (five single-slug + one combined block whose selectors list all three remaining slugs), not "eight + three byte-identical copies" — corrected; the dead-code conclusion itself verified clean. (3) Omission fixed: the gallery runtime half — per-page inline `openLightbox` implementations, lightbox modal markup (`.lightbox-modal`, `lakewood-privacy-fence.html` uses `.lightbox`), and `site.js` `wireGalleryTriggers()` dispatching to `window.openLightbox`.

**Loop status:** round 3 not clean (2 Majors + 1 runtime bug + 1 Nit). Each fresh swarm keeps reaching deeper, more obscure corners — findings are trending toward dead code and edge cases rather than wrong facts about the main architecture. Cap is 5 rounds per the sharpening loop.

- **EGM.md:** (1) The cache-busting invariant has an undocumented exception — the `thank-you.html` guard at `build.py` line 371 covers the entire head-treatment block (372–380), not just the header/footer swap, so `dist/thank-you.html` ships unversioned `site.css`/`site.js` references (verified in dist) — the exact stale-asset failure the invariant warns about. Documented and flagged for triage. (2) `check_links.py` also validates `og:image` meta content values (lines 77–78) — added. (3) `netlify.toml`'s `[build]` section (`publish = "dist"`, `command = "python3 build.py"`) was undocumented — added.
- **blog:** the `.blog-index` fold-in block sits under its own `/* blog/index.html */` marker (line 165), not the "identical styles for" markers — corrected.
- **case-studies:** (1) **Second runtime bug found and verified** — `lakewood-privacy-fence.html`'s lightbox can neither open nor close in the built site: its inline `openLightbox(card)` takes the card element (not `(imgSrc, caption)`), the build converts its cards into triggers with no `src`/`data-lightbox-src` so the site.js dispatch never fires, its modal uses `.lightbox` (not `.lightbox-modal`) so the close path can't match, and the build strips its inline `closeLightbox` handlers (build.py:322). Documented and flagged for triage. (2) "Pages carry only `case-study-cta`" false for lakewood (carries neither) — corrected. (3) "Styled by the site-wide rules" corrected: all 11 pages have their own inline `<style>` blocks with a different class vocabulary. (4) Omission fixed: the `data-gallery-*` → `switchCasePhoto` path is permanently inert (no page defines the function or carries the markup).

**Running tally of production issues flagged for human triage (not fixed — EGM phase boundary):**
1. `seasonal-landscape-cleanup.html:326` — relative lightbox path → 404 (round 3)
2. `lakewood-privacy-fence.html` — lightbox cannot open or close in dist (round 4)
3. `thank-you.html` — ships unversioned asset refs; stale-asset risk (round 4)

**Loop status:** round 4 not clean. Cap is 5; one round remains. Findings continue to arrive but are concentrated in lakewood's broken gallery and dead-code documentation — the core architecture claims have been stable since round 2.

## Production fixes applied 2026-11-05 (user-approved, after round 4)

All three triage items were fixed and verified in a fresh build (`python3 build.py`, 36 pages, `check_links.py --quiet` passing):

1. `seasonal-landscape-cleanup.html:326` — lightbox path made root-absolute; dist now carries `data-lightbox-src="/img/..."`.
2. `lakewood-privacy-fence.html` — aligned with the standard gallery pattern: six card handlers now pass explicit `(src, caption)`, the inline `openLightbox` takes `(imgSrc, caption)`, and the modal uses `.lightbox-modal` / `.lightbox-close` classes so site.js's dispatch and close paths work. Dist verified: 6 triggers with `data-lightbox-src`, modal classes present.
3. `thank-you.html` — `build.py`'s strip-and-inject block now runs outside the thank-you guard; dist verified shipping `site.css?v=…` / `site.js?v=…`.

Contracts updated to describe the fixed state. Round 5 audits the post-fix tree.
